steps.home: Every key has a home: its tonic. Stop a melody there and it feels finished; stop anywhere else and it feels like there’s more to come. “Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star” is in {c} major, and its last note is {c}.
steps.listen: The key’s chord plays, then a short melody. Listen to its last note.
steps.pull: Some degrees pull harder than others. Degree 7 sits a half step below the tonic and wants to rise to it. Degree 2 tends to step down to it. Degree 5 is steadier: it can wait.
steps.hearDegree: Hear the key’s chord, then one note. Which degree is it? Notice how much it pulls toward the tonic.
steps.build: Now find those degrees yourself, starting from the tonic.
